x: Belgrave men, it seemed, were everywhere, and if all had been eligible to score we would have won the team event; as it was we missed third place by one point and were only eight points behind Metropolitan Walking Club, the winners. George Coleman added to his list of triumphs and missed the course record held by R.

Stan Vickers led from the start, followed by George Coleman and at the mile they were 6 m.56s. and 7 m. 3s. respectively. Although Coleman got within 60 yds. of Stan, he could get no nearer and Stan went on to a meeting record of 8 mls. 120 yds.
Eric Hall carried off the 1960 Championship in a course record time of 2:39:07, to lower George Coleman's record (made in the 1955 "National") by 61secs.

However, George Coleman walked well in the final to finish 5th to Mikaelson of Sweden. The 50,000 metre Walk was more satisfying with Dordoni of Italy prevailing over Dolezal of Czechoslovakia with Britain's G.B.R.
